archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide linear aggro that kills by trigger rather than by combat: Edgar's eminence mints a body for every Vampire spell cast from the command zone, three replacement-effect doublers multiply that body, and FOUR each-opponent payoffs — Purphoros, God of the Forge, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Corpse Knight — convert every creature entry into damage or life loss at all three seats at once. Combat is the second kill, nine lords and anthems its multiplier and Cathars' Crusade its accelerant. Two checker-passed lifegain/lifeloss infinites (Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or with Sanguine Bond; stacks 004 and 006) are a third route that assembles in 4.6% of games and is priced accordingly.

role_assignment.default_role: Beatdown, and the arithmetic says so rather than the label. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock lists the sources of inevitability as superior late-game card quality, an engine that scales, an unanswerable finisher, or more answers than the table has threats. The only unanswerable finisher in the 100 is the Bloodthirsty Conqueror pairing, and goldfish measures a complete pair drawn in 4.6% of games (2.6% by turn six; 25.0% and 15.3% counting the three unrestricted tutors as wildcards). A finisher that arrives one game in twenty is not ownership of the long game, so per strategy:whos-the-beatdown the deck that loses the long game must be the beatdown. What lets the racing plan survive strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's ~120-life objection is that the payoffs are each-opponent effects rather than combat damage: a converter is in hand in 52.5% of games at a mean turn of 3.28, 42.3% by turn six, and one trigger hits all three seats simultaneously. Role stays seat-relative (strategy:multiplayer.pod-management): a board of first-strike, deathtouch and lifelink bodies plays defence against one opponent while the entry triggers race the other two.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Three named events, in the order they usually arrive. (1) A converter resolves onto a board that already holds a multiplier — the GO-WIDE KILL target, 40.2% assembled and 27.5% by turn six, mean turn 4.53 — because from that moment every cheap Vampire cast is a burn spell aimed at the table rather than a body waiting on a combat step. strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire prices cards in damage; here the rate is set by how many doublers are down, not by how many creatures survive. (2) Edgar resolving, median turn 6 and only 52.3% by turn six: he adds first strike, haste and a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire at declare, which is the alpha-strike window and not the moment the engine starts. (3) Bloodthirsty Conqueror landing while Vito or Sanguine Bond is already on the battlefield — deploy the second half only into the window strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window describes, since Conqueror is a creature and every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed creature removal (stacks 004 and 006 both say so on the record). Sequence the scariest piece last (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection): Impact Tremors and Corpse Knight read as durdle at two mana, and a 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire does not.

engines.piece: Edgar Markov (eminence) + Anointed Procession + Mondrak, Glory Dominus + Elspeth, Storm Slayer
engines.engine: The ignition, and the only component that never fails to assemble: eminence functions from the command zone, so every other Vampire spell cast mints a 1/1 from turn one whether or not Edgar is castable — which matters when his median cast is turn six. Three replacement-effect doublers multiply that single token event. Stack 002 puts the arithmetic on the record: two doublers take one token to four, each replacement effect gets exactly one bite at the event, the order you apply them cannot change the answer, and eminence does not re-trigger on the tokens (created, not cast).
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (checker pass — 1->2->4 through two doublers, order-independent); deck-facts roles doubler:tokens 3; goldfish 'A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn' 78.2% assembled / 67.9% by turn six, mean turn 2.68; goldfish mean_bodies_by_turn 1.699 at t3, 4.103 at t6, 6.593 at t10

engines.piece: Purphoros, God of the Forge + Impact Tremors + Warleader's Call + Corpse Knight
engines.engine: The conversion layer, four cards deep, and the deck's whole answer to the 1-to-3 problem: each creature entering costs EVERY opponent life, so board width is spent on all three seats at once and never has to survive to a combat step. Stack 009 verifies the layer composing on cards that are all in the 100: one {B}{B} Vampire cast into Anointed Procession and three of these payoffs makes three entry occurrences, nine separate triggers, and exactly 12 damage per opponent — lethal to a pod at 12 with zero margin. Two structural notes the pilot should carry. Purphoros deals damage and is usually not a creature at this deck's devotion, which costs a body and costs the trigger nothing; Corpse Knight causes life LOSS rather than damage, which is the clause Bloodletter of Aclazotz's replacement effect speaks to. Corpse Knight is a Zombie Knight, so casting it makes no eminence token and the lords do not pump it — it is a converter, not a Vampire.
engines.evidence: verified stack 009 (checker pass — nine triggers, 12 damage per opponent, exactly lethal at 12); verified stack 008 (checker pass — five Purphoros triggers off one two-mana Vampire through two doublers, 10 damage per opponent); oracle text (Purphoros 'deals 2 damage to each opponent', Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call 'deals 1 damage to each opponent', Corpse Knight 'each opponent loses 1 life'); goldfish 'TOKEN -> DAMAGE drawn' 52.5% assembled / 42.3% by turn six, mean turn 3.28

engines.piece: Cathars' Crusade + Abzan Falconer + Vampire Socialite + Edgar Markov's attack trigger
engines.engine: The counter layer, which turns entries into stats the way the converters turn entries into damage. Cathars' Crusade puts a +1/+1 counter on your whole board every time a creature enters, so one doubled eminence trigger grows the team once per token; Vampire Socialite has every other Vampire enter with an extra counter while an opponent has lost life this turn — a condition the converters satisfy on their own; Edgar's attack trigger adds a counter to each Vampire at declare; and Abzan Falconer gives flying to every creature carrying a counter. It is also the deck's quiet sweeper insurance: counters are what keep a token board out of -X/-X range.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all four); deck-facts roles buff:counters 10, buff:pump 10, payoff:counters 4; deck-audit threat-density 11 copies against a floor of 3

engines.piece: The lord package: Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain, Captivating Vampire, Vampire Socialite, Cordial Vampire, Drana, Liberator of Malakir, Sanctum Seeker, Shared Animosity, Abzan Falconer, Patchwork Banner
engines.engine: The combat kill, and the deck's fastest-assembling component. Lords are multiplicative against a token board in a way anthems are not against a fair one — each +1/+1 is paid nine or ten times over. Shared Animosity is the sharpest version, giving each attacker +1/+0 for every other attacker sharing a type, which on a Vampire board is quadratic. Patchwork Banner doubles as an anthem and a source of any colour.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all ten); deck-facts roles payoff:typal 2, buff:pump 10; goldfish 'A Vampire lord or anthem drawn (the combat plan)' 83.2% assembled / 72.8% by turn six, mean turn 2.60 — the best-assembling component in the deck

engines.piece: Sanctum Seeker + Bloodletter of Aclazotz + Throne of the God-Pharaoh + Twilight Prophet + Bontu's Monument
engines.engine: The attack-and-tap drain: a second, independent axis from the entry triggers, converting width into each-opponent life loss without anything dying or entering a graveyard. Sanctum Seeker pays per attacking Vampire, Throne per tapped creature at your end step, Bontu's Monument per creature spell cast, and Bloodletter doubles each opponent's loss during your turn — your own gain is never doubled, because the clause replaces only an opponent's loss. Stack 007 is the bound, and it is a refutation as much as a rate: fourteen per opponent at end step is reach, not a table-kill.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (checker pass — seven attacking Vampires under Sanctum Seeker with Bloodletter out drain 14 per opponent at declare-attackers, before blockers); verified stack 007 (checker pass, PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill — seven tapped creatures drain 14 each at end step, leaving a 15-life opponent alive at exactly 1)

engines.piece: Bloodthirsty Conqueror + Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose + Sanguine Bond
engines.engine: The deterministic kill, layered onto the primary plan rather than bolted beside it. Conqueror gains you life whenever an opponent loses life — a condition every converter trigger, every Sanctum Seeker attack and every Throne end step already satisfies — and Vito or Sanguine Bond turns that gain back into loss. Both pairings are verified table-kills at mana value needed 0, retargetable on each iteration, and the chain survives a targeted opponent's death. Their rent is honest for two of three: Conqueror is a 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire and Vito a three-mana Vampire body, so each is an eminence trigger and a lord target on the nineteen games in twenty the loop never happens; Sanguine Bond is five mana, no body, no creature type and no contribution to width, and it is the one slot the token plan genuinely subsidises.
engines.evidence: verified stacks 004 and 006 (both checker pass — deterministic table-kills); combo_details via deck-facts: 2 contained lines, both two-card infinites, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 0, popularity 64824 and 54630; deck-audit engine block names Bloodthirsty Conqueror as the deck's ONE single point of failure, measured 4.6% assembled / 2.6% by turn six, mean turn 5.50

engines.piece: Caretaker's Talent + Welcoming Vampire + Preacher of the Schism + Twilight Prophet + Night's Whisper
engines.engine: Refill that is board-gated by design: Caretaker's Talent draws whenever one or more tokens enter (once a turn) and at level two copies a token, Welcoming Vampire draws when small creatures enter, Preacher draws or mints a lifelink Vampire on attack depending on who is at the top of the life totals, Twilight Prophet drains and refills once you control ten permanents. Only Night's Whisper draws without a board. This is the axis to name honestly rather than smooth over: the taxonomy counts three copies against a template's ten, the simulation's group is five, and every card in it needs the swarm to already exist. A deck that draws only when it is ahead has no refill on the turn it most needs one — after a sweeper.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all five); deck-audit card-advantage 3 copies (Caretaker's Talent, Night's Whisper, Welcoming Vampire) against a target of >=10, verdict UNDER, with its own note listing Castle Locthwain, Henrika Domnathi, Midgar, Minas Tirith, Preacher of the Schism, Savai Triome, Silent Clearing and Sunbaked Canyon as functions the taxonomy files elsewhere; goldfish 'A draw engine drawn' 60.3% assembled / 49.2% by turn six

engines.piece: Charismatic Conqueror + Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fort + Mavren Fein, Dusk Apostle + Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage + Ocelot Pride + Elenda, the Dusk Rose
engines.engine: Token width that does not cost a card from hand, which is what keeps the converters fed between Vampire casts. Charismatic Conqueror taxes every untapped artifact or creature the table plays — they tap it or you get a lifelink Vampire — so it makes tokens on other people's turns and scales with three opponents' development rather than yours. Legion's Landing is a one-mana token that becomes a repeatable token land after any three-creature attack; Mavren Fein pays on every attack; Bloodline Keeper makes a 2/2 flier every turn for no cards; Ocelot Pride copies every token that entered this turn once you hold the city's blessing; Elenda converts any creature death into a pile of lifelink Vampires equal to her power, and Cathars' Crusade and Cordial Vampire both grow her.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all six); deck-facts roles threat:tokens 10; goldfish counts Charismatic Conqueror, Legion's Landing, Mavren Fein, Bloodline Keeper and Ocelot Pride inside the 78.2% multiplier-or-extra-token-maker group

engines.piece: Teferi's Protection + Akroma's Will + Flawless Maneuver + Boros Charm + Deflecting Swat + Swiftfoot Boots
engines.engine: Board-wide insurance sized for a deck whose plan IS a board. Four of the six protect every permanent at once rather than one creature, which is the correct shape when the thing being answered is a sweeper rather than a spot removal spell; Akroma's Will doubles as the alpha-strike enabler, and with a commander out it grants both modes. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's racing alternative is the tension worth naming: protection slots cost you every game and removal only costs you some, and this deck's engine does not route through its commander — eminence keeps running from the command zone whatever happens to Edgar.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all six); deck-audit protection 9 copies against a target of 5-7, verdict OVER; goldfish 'Protection held for the swarm' 68.1% assembled / 56.7% by turn six

candidate_missing_lines.title: All four converters on one Vampire: what does a two-mana cast cost the table?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 009 verifies three payoffs composing across three entry occurrences for nine triggers and 12 damage per opponent. Corpse Knight carries the same 'whenever another creature you control enters' condition at 1 life lost to each opponent, so the same three occurrences should read twelve triggers and 15 per opponent. The composition rule is verified; this count is not, and the mixed damage/life-loss arithmetic is exactly where a checker has bounded this deck before (stack 007).

candidate_missing_lines.title: Bloodletter of Aclazotz over the conversion layer, not just the attack step
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Bloodletter's replacement is verified twice, and both times over pure life loss: Sanctum Seeker's drain at declare-attackers (stack 003) and Throne of the God-Pharaoh's end-step loss (stack 007). Corpse Knight is the converter that causes life loss by the same route, and the three others deal damage under a reminder line reading '(Damage causes loss of life.)' The doubling of a damage-sourced loss is unverified on this deck's record, and the two halves of the question may not have the same answer.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Corpse Knight as loop ignition: a token wave starting the Conqueror chain with nothing dying
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stacks 004 and 006 verify the loop from a stated life-loss seed. Corpse Knight makes every creature entry a life-loss event at all three seats at once, which should feed Conqueror's 'whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life' with no combat, no death and no targeting. The loop is verified; this ignition source is not, and the three simultaneous seat losses producing three separate Conqueror triggers is the part that needs resolving.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Cathars' Crusade into Abzan Falconer: does one doubled entry give the whole board flying?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Cathars' Crusade puts a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control whenever a creature enters, and Abzan Falconer's static ability gives flying to each creature you control with a counter on it. A doubled eminence trigger is two entry occurrences, so the board should acquire counters twice and then be flying — including the entering tokens themselves, if the Crusade trigger resolves while they are on the battlefield. The interaction of a static grant with counters landing at different times, and whether Edgar's declare-attackers counters arrive before blockers are declared, is the whole question.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The third doubler: does one eminence trigger make eight bodies?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 002 verifies 1->2->4 through two replacement effects and that the application order is immaterial. All three doublers are in the 100 and each reads that twice as many of those tokens are created instead, so a third application should read 1->2->4->8 as one entry event. The arithmetic is an extrapolation from a verified line rather than the verified line itself, and eight entry occurrences under four converters is the deck's ceiling turn.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Ocelot Pride's copy clause through the doublers
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: With the city's blessing, Ocelot Pride copies every token that entered this turn at your end step — a create effect, so each doubler in play should replace it. combo_details records three near-infinite token lines built on exactly these four cards plus Satya, Aetherflux Genius, so the shape is recognised in the corpus; the question is what one end step is worth here without the missing card. Whether it is a loop or a large finite number, the resulting entries feed four converters.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Elenda dying into the doublers
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Elenda creates X 1/1 lifelink Vampire tokens on death where X is her power, and Cathars' Crusade plus Cordial Vampire both grow her while the board develops. Those tokens are created, so the doublers should replace the event, and the resulting simultaneous entries should trigger every converter. This makes a sweeper into a conversion turn rather than a loss, which is the single most valuable thing a linear deck can own — and none of it is verified.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The trap the go-wide label implies only half applies, because the machine is not made of creatures. Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Cathars' Crusade, Caretaker's Talent, Patchwork Banner, Herald's Horn, Legion's Landing, Elspeth and an indestructible, usually-noncreature Purphoros all survive a creature wrath, and eminence rebuilds from the command zone with no recast tax and no card spent. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math says assume the wrath over four players, deploy in waves, and buy resilience rather than restraint — here the resilience is bought at the permanent layer rather than the body layer, so commit exactly the width that wins now and keep the next multiplier in hand. Two exposures to state plainly. Cathars' Crusade counters are what keep a token board out of -X/-X range, so the toughness-based sweeper is worse for you than the destroy-based one. And the refill is board-gated (three counted draw sources, five in the simulation's group), so the turn after a wrath is the turn this deck draws least — strategy:card-advantage's balance rule puts card advantage in charge of exactly that late game. Four board-wide protection instants at 68.1% mean the pivot turn can be insured; Teferi's Protection answers the wrath and the counterattack together.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Structurally the deck's best matchup and the pilot should know it. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial says taxes attack velocity math directly and that you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown racing the lock's completion. Eminence is the exception a tax cannot reach: it is a triggered ability from the command zone, not a cast, so every Vampire spell still pays double under a Sphere. The curve cooperates — 8 one-drops and 17 two-drops out of 63 spells, modal mana value 3 — and two cost reducers (Herald's Horn, Bontu's Monument) lower the bill rather than raising sources, which on a curve this cheap is the same purchase. Edgar at six mana is the first thing a tax prices out and the deck does not need him on the battlefield. Name your outs early per strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs: the piece that beats you is the one stopping tokens from entering or taxing creature spells, not the flashiest lock piece — and note that Cavern of Souls' coloured mana casts creature spells only, so it cannot pay for an activated ability under a tax.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Re-ask the role (strategy:whos-the-beatdown): against a faster deck you are the control, and this deck can take that seat without changing plans. Thirty creature entries, lifelink tokens from Legion's Landing, Charismatic Conqueror and Mavren Fein, first strike from Edgar, Stromkirk Captain, Ocelot Pride and Cemetery Gatekeeper, deathtouch from Preacher of the Schism, Vampire of the Dire Moon and a 5/5 flying Conqueror make a board that blanks an attack step — strategy:card-advantage.virtual's exact point, that a wide board turns their small creatures into dead cards without drawing anything. Charismatic Conqueror taxes their development on the way in and Olivia's Wrath is a one-sided sweeper against a non-Vampire board. Spend life freely above the threshold where it buys tempo — the manabase asks for it, with Ancient Tomb, Mana Confluence, Caves of Koilos, Silent Clearing, Sunbaked Canyon and three fetches all charging life, and Anguished Unmaking charging three more — but track each opponent's clock separately, because 40 life attacked from three directions is not 40 life (strategy:multiplayer.pod-management).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: You are the clock and the deck is fast enough to be one: a lord or anthem at a mean turn of 2.60, a multiplier at 2.68, a converter at 3.28. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's standard cuts both ways — the table applies 'does this card win the game if it resolves' to your presentation too, so count the table's open mana before committing and prefer the win attempt that leaves a rebuilt position if it fails. Here the conversion plan is the one that does: a removed multiplier costs a card, an interrupted alpha strike costs a board. Twelve interaction copies against an aggro template's five to six is defensible against combo specifically (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: the bar is 'ends the game or ends my deck's function'), but strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry still binds — hold the one-for-ones until the threat is pointed at you or you are paying a card to protect two bystanders. The genuinely thin place is the noncreature answer: two cards, in hand in 30.8% of games and 23.8% by turn six, against three opponents any of whom can present a noncreature engine you cannot touch.

distribution_notes: Copies, not entries: 100 copies across 97 entries — 37 land copies in 34 entries, 63 spells. Curve (nonland) 8 / 17 / 20 / 12 / 5 / 1 across mana values 1-6, modal 3, nothing at 7+. strategy:deckbuilding.curve reports the format's modal mana value at 2 from EDHREC data, so this list sits one step above the shape, which is worth watching in a deck whose plan wants two spells a turn. Roles: threat:body 30, threat:tokens 10, doubler:tokens 3, buff:counters 10, buff:pump 10, wincon:drain 8, wincon:combat 3, payoff:counters 4, payoff:typal 2; taxonomy coverage 100% with no unclassified card. deck-audit puts creatures (30) inside the 26-32 aggro band, threat-density at 11 against a floor of 3, consistency 0.925 on the turn-3 land drop, interaction breadth at 5 of 5 classes, and bracket floor 4 (Optimized) driven by four Game Changers — Ancient Tomb, Demonic Tutor, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor — with combo content forcing only 3 and the two-card infinites independently forcing 4. Three axes read under target. Colour-sources is -10 on black and is the real one: black carries 49.4% of the deck's coloured pips (38 pips across 28 cards, up to three at once, wanted from turn one) on 41.8% of its coloured sources, and 23 land sources against the 36 Karsten's 90% column asks for. Red runs the opposite way at 14.3% of pips on 25.5% of sources, never more than one pip and never before turn two; white nearly agrees with itself at 36.4% against 32.7%. On-curve from lands alone: W 0.849, R 0.762, B 0.667; five rocks lift those to 0.895 / 0.831 / 0.742 and black's total to 26. strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources reads those numbers as a budget rather than a table, and 36 black sources inside a 37-land deck is arithmetic that does not exist — read the gap as sequencing posture, not a shopping list. Ramp is 7 against 10-12. Card-advantage is 3 against 10 and that is a genuine cost rather than a taxonomy artefact: the counted three are Caretaker's Talent, Night's Whisper and Welcoming Vampire, the simulation's group of five adds Preacher of the Schism and Twilight Prophet, and every one of them except Night's Whisper needs a board before it draws. Two axes read over: interaction 12 against an aggro target of 5-6, and protection 9 against 5-7, which is the defensible over-count since four of the nine protect every permanent at once. Interaction BREADTH is at target with all five classes covered and nothing uncovered — the thinness is depth, at 11 creature answers against 2 artifact, 2 enchantment, 1 graveyard and 2 land, which is why the goldfish noncreature-answer figure (30.8% assembled, 23.8% by turn six, off Despark and Anguished Unmaking) is the number that binds rather than the axis verdict. Lands: 15 of 37 can enter tapped (41%, over the one-in-three budget) but only three do so unconditionally — Nomad Outpost, Savai Triome and Midgar, City of Mako. One restricted source, Cavern of Souls, whose coloured mana casts creature spells only and therefore cannot pay for Castle Locthwain's draw, Bloodline Keeper's flip or Captivating Vampire's steal; its colourless mode still can. Openers: first sevens keep at 81.8%, mean mulligans 0.215, land drops 99.9% on turn two and 92.5% on turn three. One engine component rests on a single card — Bloodthirsty Conqueror — and strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices a named card at 7.1% of an opening seven, which is the ceiling on that line rather than a defect in the simulation. Two internal frictions worth naming. Olivia's Wrath gives each NON-Vampire creature -X/-X for X equal to your Vampire count, and five of the deck's thirty creatures are not Vampires — Corpse Knight, Abzan Falconer, Ocelot Pride, Mondrak and Purphoros when devotion makes it a creature — so the deck's own one-sided sweeper kills a converter, a doubler and the flying enabler, and Cathars' Crusade counters are the mitigation. And the synergy graph contributes nothing here: all 33 of its intra-deck edges are lands pointing at Herald's Horn under a 'Ramp + Cost Reduction' rule, which is what deck-facts means when it says the graph is a global top-10 shortlist and not a per-deck fit score.
overall_assessment: This is a linear critical-mass deck (strategy:critical-mass) whose threshold is a number of creature entries, and whose defining property is that those entries never have to survive a combat step. Edgar's eminence is an ignition that runs from the command zone in 100% of games; three replacement-effect doublers make each ignition multiplicative rather than additive; and four payoffs turn every resulting entry into damage or life loss at all three seats. That last layer is the whole answer to strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's charge against aggro — incremental combat damage cannot get through ~120 life behind three defences, but 'each opponent loses life' scales with exactly the width the engine was already producing, and the conversion layer is in hand in 52.5% of games at a mean turn of 3.28, with a multiplier alongside it in 40.2%. Stack 009 is the piece of evidence the deck's world-view actually rests on: one {B}{B} Vampire, one doubler, three payoffs, nine triggers, 12 damage per opponent — the primary plan verified on its own terms rather than the deck's lottery ticket verified in its place. Default role is beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown), and the reason is arithmetic rather than temperament: strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's test for inevitability is an unanswerable finisher or an engine that scales past the table, and the deterministic kill is drawn in 4.6% of games naturally, 25.0% with the three unrestricted tutors modelled as wildcards. Keeping Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito and Sanguine Bond is right on strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's layering clause rather than its finisher count: Conqueror's trigger condition is fed by every converter trigger, every Sanctum Seeker attack and every Throne end step the deck already produces, so the pieces overlap the primary plan instead of forming an unconnected second one. What they buy is two verified table-kills at mana value needed 0 plus a 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire and a three-mana Vampire body that pay rent as eminence triggers and lord targets. What they cost is one slot, and it should be named exactly: Sanguine Bond, five mana, no body, no creature type, no width. The deck this makes is an aggro deck holding a lottery ticket, not a combo deck with a fair backup, and that ordering should govern every sequencing decision — race with the entries, present the loop only into a window strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window would sanction, and never slow the board to protect a pairing that appears one game in twenty. Two tensions are live and neither is cosmetic. Black is the short colour against the heaviest pip load, 23 land sources against a 36-source yardstick and a 66.7% on-curve rate from lands alone, which is the colour of the one-drops and the {B}{B} two-drops the engine is built on. And the refill is board-gated — three counted draw sources, five in the simulation's group, only one of which draws without a board — so the deck draws least on precisely the turn a sweeper makes it need cards most. strategy:critical-mass is blunt that a linear deck's defence is speed, redundancy and resilience rather than answers; twelve interaction copies against a five-or-six template is the deck spending on answers in a colour budget that is already overdrawn, and the honest reading is that the converter group of four is where a slot buys the most, because strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors puts five copies at 31% of openers and this list's thinnest load-bearing class sits below that.
gaps: No section on go-wide / token strategy as such. The best-matching query for 'go wide tokens anthem' returns strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources at 0.144 — i.e. nothing. The doc has nothing on token doubling as a multiplicative rather than additive resource, on why replacement-effect doublers compound while anthems add, or on the ordering rule that makes several doublers order-independent. This deck's entire plan is that arithmetic.

No section on converting board width into non-combat damage. 'Whenever a creature you control enters, each opponent loses life' is the single most important effect class here and the corpus can only reach it through strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire, a burn-deck frame about cards-as-damage, and one unpriced clause in strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry. A section on trigger-based kills versus combat kills — sweeper exposure, evasion irrelevance, the payoff living on a noncreature permanent, and the difference between a payoff that deals damage and one that causes life loss — would be load-bearing for every token deck.

No section on typal critical mass. Best query score 0.411, and that is strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite matching on the word 'type'. Lords are multiplicative against a wide board and additive against a fair one; typal cost reduction is a rebate on nearly every cast; a creature-type commitment narrows the pool in exchange for a scaling rate; and a typal sweeper like Olivia's Wrath is one-sided only to the extent the deck stays on-type. strategy:critical-mass covers linear decks generally and nothing about the typal case.

No treatment of the combo half that pays rent. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density carries Eisenherz's layering clause and a two-combos rule, both framed for cEDH. There is no guidance on the common Commander decision this deck faces: when one combo half is also a fine fair card and the other is a five-mana blank, how should each slot be priced against a plan it does not otherwise serve?

Nothing on rebuilding after a sweeper when the engine is noncreature and the draw is board-gated. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math is about sizing commitment and holding a rebuild package in hand; it has no frame for a deck whose machine outlives the board, whose rebuild is a free trigger from the command zone, and whose card draw switches off at exactly the moment the board does. The correct commitment level and the correct draw count are both different in that case.

No section on trigger timing inside combat — specifically whether +1/+1 counters or granted abilities arriving from a declare-attackers trigger are visible to a static ability before blockers are declared. Two candidate lines here turn on it, and strategy:combat-math.racing addresses clocks rather than steps.
